sources.publisher: Government of Georgia via UNECE/WHO Protocol on Water and Health
sources.note: Food Safety Agency is identified as drinking-water control body; small rural systems were included. The report narrative gives 37% for 2021-2022, 44.5% for 2023 and 40.3% for 2024; Table 4.i lists E. coli non-compliance at 25% (2005), 34% (2019) and 40.3% (2024). The 2024 table and narrative share a number but have distinct indicator contexts; no explicit crosswalk is supplied. Sample denominator and urban/rural breakdown are blank. Percentages are not population coverage.

sources.publisher: Government of Georgia / National Environmental Agency
sources.note: Resolution No.424 establishes a state accounting system for fresh drinking-water extraction wells deeper than 20 m drilled after the regulation takes effect; pre-existing wells and mineral/thermal/medicinal waters are outside the legal scope. NEA separately states that household wells are excluded. The required passport includes coordinates and owner identity/contact data; field/laboratory results are attached only when sampling was performed. The regulation requires an NEA hydrogeological database but no public API, public access terms or de-identified export was verified.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia
sources.note: Catalogue record NEA122 lists the point-geometry Groundwater monitoring layer Groundwtaer_Monitoring_Stations_NEA as public/free; the row lists SQL SDE server and personal-computer storage but no portal-placement URL. The layer payload, fields, coordinate reference system, active dates and reuse licence were not verified.

NEA describes automatic stations at monitored wells in Tianeti and field procedures for portable measurements, data registration, documentation and recording; no raw time series, station dictionary or reuse terms are published in the notice.

Article 32 describes the state surface/groundwater monitoring system and states that NEA provides quantitative and qualitative observation data to interested parties on request; the law separately assigns state drinking-water quality control to the National Food Safety Agency.

Direct RAR URL linked from NEA's 2026-11-26 announcement. Retrieval from this execution environment failed; archive contents, internal files, data dictionary, archive hash and reuse terms remain unverified. A failed retrieval here does not establish that the official server is generally unavailable.

sources.publisher: Experimental and Clinical Medicine Georgia (article reporting NFA secondary data analysis)
sources.note: Published figures 1-3 report national and regional aggregate sample counts/rates; raw NFA sample-level records, complete denominators, sampling design and a data dictionary are not supplied. Regional counts sum to 500 vs national 502 in 2020 and 621 vs national 599 in 2021. The article's 2023 national 49.5% is not reconciled with the UNECE/WHO report narrative 44.5%. The article's formal peer-review procedure was not independently verified from accessible journal policy pages.
